creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Fencil decision chrome-colors (owner-nodded, 2026-11-08): Muster has no theme of its own, and the redesign's new surfaces take their colors from settings that already exist.

- The agent list keeps macOS's own colors, as it does today.
- The pane area, pane headers and the conversation view included, takes the terminal's background and foreground from [colors]. A header is the background shifted a little toward the foreground, so it reads as part of the pane. The owner's config sets neither, so his headers would come from the renderer's default background.
- A tint for a state, behind a blocked row or header, is that state's agent_* color mixed into the surface it sits on, so changing agent_blocked recolors the tint too.

No color setting is added. One pure function derives every color, with a minimum contrast between text and the surface under it, and is tested against a light theme, a dark theme and the renderer's default: a computed color can lose contrast on an unusual theme, such as a light terminal beside a dark-mode sidebar. The rows, pane-header, conversation and banner cards all draw with it.
title: Derive the redesign's colors from the terminal colors, macOS and the state legend
